messages:
mike: FYI noisy 503 wave in hosted inference (us-west1) starting ~11:03. multiple customers reporting short-lived 5xx bursts :rotating_light:
anya: seeing same in grafana — gateway 503 spike, downstream inference pods returning 502/503 around KV cache hits spike
leo: linking a few request-ids: rId=usw1-8a7b, rId=usw1-8a9c, rId=usw1-8b01 — patterns look like bursts, not constant saturation
james: any deploys around that time?
deploy-bot: deploy/redwood-runtime@v2.14.1 finished at 11:01 UTC — canary 10%
sarah: canary rollout started 11:01, but traffic weighting didn't change after 11:02. not sure it's deploy-related yet
anya: KV cache miss rate jumped 11:03-11:06 simultaneously with 503s. maybe cache invalidation storm?
mike: ops: can we scale the backend pool temporarily and route traffic away from us-west1? want to reduce customer impact while we root cause
leo: scaling up dedicated pools + shifting routing to us-west2 in progress. patching route table now :hourglass_flowing_sand:
james: logs show repeated `KVCache::Get` latency hitting >200ms then timeout leading to downstream error. snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T11:03:12Z] KVCache::Get key=ctx-xyz latency=215ms status=timeout
[2026-03-17T11:03:12Z] InferenceWorker::Serve req=usw1-8a7b -> upstream_error 502
```
anya: interesting — network flaps? or overloaded cache nodes? need pod-level metrics for kv-cache cluster
sarah: I'm grabbing node metrics and nic errors now. also checking egress NAT rates, SNAT exhaustion would cause weird timeouts
mike: any customer escalations yet? support?
leo: support pinged for 4 customers with elevated error rates. letting them know we're on it and shifting traffic
james: temporarily toggled `prefix_kv_caching` to off for the problematic model shard at 11:10 — testing whether bypass reduces 5xxs
anya: after toggle, error rate dropped ~60% in the next 2 mins. looks like cache layer is culprit. great quick test
mike: good—keep that toggle. we'll treat this as mitigation. need triage plan and RCA: why did cache invalidation/miss storm happen?
leo: possible causes: a) bad cache invalidation routine after model reload, b) canary caused cache churn on shared shard, c) eviction policy bug under concurrent loads
sarah: also seeing a burst of long-tail prompt lengths from a customer at 11:02 which caused unusual KV lookups — correlating
james: created a read-only snapshot of kv-cache node logs and will run grep for `invalidate` and `reload` events between 10:55-11:05
anya: action items for immediate runbook: 1) keep prefix_kv_caching off for shard X for 24h, 2) alert threshold: KVCache miss-rate > 15% -> page SRE, 3) add histogram for KV eviction spikes to console dashboard
mike: assign owners: james -> collect logs + grep (ETA 30m), anya -> dashboards/alerts (ETA 1h), leo -> routing rollback verification + customer comms (ETA 15m), sarah -> network/infra check (ETA 30m)
leo: customer comms draft: "We're mitigating elevated 5xxs by temporarily disabling prefix caching for the affected models and shifting traffic; continuing investigation." thoughts? :thumbsup:
mike: send, mention ETA for follow-up 1h
james: grep results: found a rapid sequence of `invalidate_all` calls during canary startup at 11:01:05 -> 11:02:10 originating from runtime process id=4242. attaching lines to the incident log (copied to S3)
anya: that matches — canary may have triggered full-shard invalidation. need to patch canary rollout to use targeted invalidation only
sarah: no NIC errors or SNAT exhaustion observed. network looks stable. points more to software-triggered churn
leo: rolling canary back to previous runtime version for safety while we patch invalidation behavior :wrench:
deploy-bot: rollback/redwood-runtime@v2.14.0 initiated at 11:18 UTC by leo
mike: good. next steps for post-incident: schedule short postmortem, document runbook changes, implement targeted invalidation in runtime (priority P1), add guardrail in rollout system to prevent global invalidation during canaries
anya: I'll open a tracking ticket with proposed patches and include test plan for canary invalidation simulation
james: will pair with runtime team to reproduce invalidate storm locally — adding repro checklist: reproduce canary startup, monitor KV invalidation calls, assert no `invalidate_all` during warmup
leo: will update affected customers with a short summary and next steps in support thread
sarah: monitoring: keep caching toggle until patch is deployed and tested. recommend extended alert window + customer-facing status update at 1h
mike: thanks all. I'll be primary contact for the post-incident notes. we'll reconvene in 60m with updates. :white_check_mark:
